a b s t r a c t
An organic additive, Diazine Black (DB), was employed as a leveler for microvia filling using copper elec-
troplating. DB is a derivative of Janus Green B (JGB), which is a common leveler used for copper fill of
submicron or micron circuit metallization in electronic products. This study determined the optimal
DB concentration for achieving the best filling performance. The electrochemical behavior of DB and its
interaction with other additives, such as a suppressor and an accelerator were characterized using gal-
vanostatic measurements. These electrochemical analyses helped explaining the filling mechanism of
the plating formula containing the DB. Various surface morphologies and the crystalline orientation of
the plated copper films caused by different DB concentrations were characterized by a scanning electron
microscope (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), respectively. The corresponding chemical activity of the
surface atoms of the plated copper films caused by different DB concentrations was characterized using
a test of etching rate.

The influence ofthe additives on the surface morphology ofcop-
per deposit was observed using SEM. Fig. 7 shows the top views of
the copper deposits obtained from different plating formulas. Only
two formulas, namely,
\mathsf { P E G } + \mathsf { C l } ^ { - } + \mathsf { S P S }
and PEG + Cl− + SPS + DB, led
to a flat plane within a micron range, as shown in Fig. 7e and f. Par-
ticularly, only the formula with PEG + Cl− + SPS + DB resulted in an
overall mirror-like surface. The other formulas resulted in a marked
micron roughness on the copper deposits. In the absence of SPS,
the copper deposit had a small crystal size, as shown in Fig. 7d. The
largest copper crystal size was obtained from the plating solution
containing SPS only, as shown in Fig. 7b. In addition, the plating
formula composed of PEG, Cl−, and SPS could not give rise to a
macro flatness of copper deposit, as shown in Fig. 2c and d, but
only resulted in a local flatness within a range in micron scale, as
shown in Fig. 7e. These results give us an insight into the interaction
of these additives, which shows that DB, a nominal leveler, cannot
flatten the surface of the copper deposit by itself, and SPS, a nom-
inal brightener, cannot brighten the surface of the copper deposit.
The mirror-like copper surface results from the interaction of these
additives, which causes an equal copper growth rate in the vertical
and horizontal directions.

tation rather than the [2 2 0] orientation becomes dominant [54].
The change in the preferential orientation will lead to a change in
the chemical activity of the surface copper atoms, which can be
characterized by an etching test.

4. Conclusions
A leveler, namely DB, employed for microvia filling was tested in
this study. An excellent filling performance is obtained from a cop-
per plating formula composed of 200 ppm PEG, 60 ppm Cl−, 1 ppm
SPS, and 1 ppm DB. This plating formula not only results in BUF of
microvias but also leads to a mirror-like copper surface. According
to electrochemical analyses, the root cause for achieving BUF in the
plating solution was attributed to the CDA behavior ofthis formula.
Although DB is a derivative of JGB, their electrochemical behav-
iors are somewhat different. DB cannot enhance the suppression
of PEG–Cl on copper deposition, whereas JGB can do that. Never-
theless, DB can effectively suppress the acceleration of SPS–Cl on
copper deposition in the presence of PEG. The preferential orien-
tation of the plated copper films is changed from [1 1 1] to [2 2 0]
because of the addition of DB, which causes a decrease in the etch-
ing rate of the plated copper film and results in fine grains and
mirror-like copper surfaces.
